Working with coding agents

Source: vignettes/agents.Rmd
agents.Rmd

This article is for authors who let a coding agent, such as Claude Code, edit a weft project, and for the agents themselves. After it you will know what weft tells an agent, why, and how each kind of finding should be answered.

Why an agent needs rules

weft’s checks fail on purpose. A failed claim says that the prose and the numbers disagree. The commit gate refuses a typed number. Removing a construct needs a line in the commit message.

An agent asked to “make the render pass” has easy ways to do it that defeat the point: loosen the claim, delete the check, type the number back in as a literal, turn on draft mode, or commit with --no-verify. Each makes the error go away and leaves the report wrong. The rules below close those ways, and say what to do instead.

What use_agent_docs() writes

use_agent_docs() writes an AGENTS.md block and a skill. use_weft() runs it, or you can run it alone (see vignette("setup", package = "weft")).

The first is a block in AGENTS.md, the file many coding agents read when they start. weft appends it after any text already there:

cat(readLines(system.file("agent", "AGENTS.md", package = "weft")), sep = "\n")
## weft

This project uses the weft R package: numbers in the prose are computed
(`` `r x` ``), wording that depends on them is chosen by spans
(`[a site | # sites]{n="k"}`), and `claim()` checks what the prose says.

- A failed claim is a finding to report to the author, not an error to clear.
- Do not change or remove a check (`claim()`, a guard, a bound) to make a
  render or a commit pass, unless the author asks for exactly that.
- When a commit removes weft constructs on purpose, add the line the
  commit-msg hook prints, `Weft-Removed: N`, with its number. Do not use
  `--no-verify` to get past the hook.
- Values that hold for one chapter only go in that document's front matter
  under `weft: dict_local:`, each with a `why:`; read them as
  `dict_local$key`, never `dict$key`.

The weft skill is in the project's skills folders (`.agents/skills/weft/`,
`.claude/skills/weft/`) and has the detail; `weft::agent_docs()` prints it.

In the project, the block sits between a <!-- weft:start ... --> line and a <!-- weft:end --> line. weft replaces only what lies between them. Claude Code reads CLAUDE.md, not AGENTS.md. If the project has a CLAUDE.md, add the line @AGENTS.md to it so that it includes the block.

The second is a skill, weft/SKILL.md, which a coding agent loads when a task touches a weft document or a weft report. It sits in each skills folder (see the next section), with two files in references/, syntax.md and reports.md:

cat(readLines(system.file("agent", "SKILL.md", package = "weft")), sep = "\n")
---
name: weft
description: Use when editing a document of a project that uses the weft R package (inline `r` values, spans with n=, if=, sign=, list=, cite=, claim() checks, _weft.yml), or when a render, a lint or a commit fails with a weft report.
metadata:
  weft-version: "@VERSION@"
---

# weft

weft keeps the numbers in a manuscript computed and the wording that depends
on them chosen by the numbers. This file is written by `weft::use_agent_docs()`.

## References

`references/syntax.md` has the constructs, one example each; `references/reports.md`
shows how to read a failed render, a lint report and a refused commit.
`weft::agent_docs()` lists them, and `Rscript -e "weft::agent_docs('syntax')"` (or
`'reports'`) prints the installed package's version of each; it wins if the copy
here is older.

## The four rules

- A failed claim is a finding to report to the author, not an error to clear.
- Do not change or remove a check (`claim()`, a guard, a bound) to make a
  render or a commit pass, unless the author asks for exactly that.
- When a commit removes weft constructs on purpose, add the line the
  commit-msg hook prints, `Weft-Removed: N`, with its number. Do not use
  `--no-verify` to get past the hook.
- Values that hold for one chapter only go in that document's front matter
  under `weft: dict_local:`, each with a `why:`; read them as
  `dict_local$key`, never `dict$key`.

## Reading a failed-claim report

The report gives the line, the expression, the check and the value. Say
which of the check and the value looks wrong and why. Do not decide: the author does. Never edit the
check or the value to make the claim true.

## The trailer

A removal on purpose needs the hook's number: `git commit --trailer "Weft-Removed: N"`.
A wrong number is refused.

## Findings added at a commit

The hook refuses a commit that adds findings. Fix each one at its source:
- a typed number: compute it and write the value (`r x`), or put it in the
  dictionary (`dict.yml`);
- a literal that must stay: mark it with `.weft-literal` and give a real `why`.

## dict_local

- It lives in one document's front matter under `weft: dict_local:`.
- Each key has a `why:` saying why it is not in `dict.yml`.
- Read it as `dict_local$key`; `dict$key` does not see it.
- A key that two documents need belongs in `dict.yml`.

## Draft mode

With `draft: true` (or `WEFT_DRAFT`) a render passes everything. `verify()`
refuses a draft, and the commit gate ignores it and judges every commit as
usual. Do not leave a project in draft mode to get a result.

## Before you commit and before you hand back

- `weft::lints()` before a commit: it lists every finding. `weft::gate()`
  judges the staged commit as the hook does.
- `weft::verify()` before handing work back: it renders and checks the claims.
<!-- weft-file: use_agent_docs @VERSION@ @HASH@ -->

In the project, the placeholders (the version in metadata and the last line, and the hash) hold the weft version and a hash, so that use_agent_docs() can tell whether you have edited the file.

Which tools read which folder: skills

The skill format is the same for every tool; the tools differ in the folder they scan. use_agent_docs(skills = ) takes preset names or folders relative to the project root, and writes the same files into each:

preset folder read by
agents .agents/skills Gemini CLI; reported for Codex, opencode and Cursor
claude .claude/skills Claude Code
codex .agents/skills reported for Codex
gemini .gemini/skills Gemini CLI
opencode .opencode/skills reported for opencode
kimi .kimi-code/skills Kimi Code
cursor .cursor/skills reported for Cursor

The default is "agents", which writes .agents/skills alone. Claude Code reads .claude/skills/ and not .agents/skills/, so Claude Code users pass skills = c("agents", "claude"), or install the plugin with /plugin marketplace add vorpalvorpal/weft. A .claude/skills/weft copy that an earlier weft wrote is left as it is by the default call; the closing message says that it was not updated and gives that call to update it, and status() names it. That Codex, opencode and Cursor read .agents/skills is reported by secondary sources; it was not checked against the vendors’ documents. A folder of your own is a path such as "tools/skills"; an absolute path or one with .. is an error. skills = character() writes only the AGENTS.md block. Gemini CLI reads GEMINI.md, so if the project has one, add the line @AGENTS.md to it; the call says so.

The copies in a project can be older than the installed package. weft::agent_docs() lists the documents and weft::agent_docs("syntax") prints the installed version of one.

Installing the skill without a project

To give the skill to Claude Code for yourself, in every project, install the plugin from the GitHub repository. In a Claude Code session:

/plugin marketplace add vorpalvorpal/weft
/plugin install weft@weft

or in one step, on Claude Code 2.1.275 or later:

/plugin install weft --marketplace vorpalvorpal/weft

From a shell, claude plugin marketplace add vorpalvorpal/weft then claude plugin install weft@weft do the same. Cross-tool installers that read a skills/<name>/SKILL.md folder from a repository can read skills/weft/ from vorpalvorpal/weft.

A copy installed this way belongs to you, not to a project. It is not updated with the R package, so it can fall behind the installed weft; update it from Claude Code, or run weft::agent_docs() to read the current text. The copy that use_agent_docs() writes into the project is the one status() checks.

The four rules

A failed claim is a finding, not an error

When a claim fails, the sentence, the check and the value disagree. One of them is wrong, and only the author knows which. Here a draft says all sites met the guideline, and one did not:

writeLines(c(
  "---",
  "title: \"Survey\"",
  "output: md_document",
  "knitr:",
  "  opts_knit:",
  "    weft: !expr weft::weft_setup()",
  "---",
  "",
  "```{r data}",
  "ntu <- c(Upper = 4.2, Middle = 7.9, Lower = 12.6)",
  "```",
  "",
  "All sites were below the guideline, with a highest reading of `r claim(max(ntu), . < 10)`."
), "survey.Rmd")
r <- tryCatch(rmarkdown::render("survey.Rmd", quiet = TRUE),
              error = function(e) cat(conditionMessage(e), "\n"))
#> weft: 1 claim failed
#>   survey.Rmd:13  `r claim(max(ntu), . < 10)`
#>       . < 10 was FALSE (value 12.6)
#> Read each sentence. If FALSE is right, rewrite the sentence.
#> Do not loosen a claim to clear this.

The agent should report this to the author, with its reading of which part looks wrong. Here the data look right, so the sentence is wrong. It should not:

  • change the check to . < 15;
  • delete the claim();
  • edit the data to fit.

The author may still choose any of these. The rule is that the agent does not choose for them.

Do not change a check to make something pass

A check is a claim(), an if guard on a span, or a bound such as the one in . < 10. Removing or loosening one to clear a failure needs the author’s explicit request for exactly that change.

Removed constructs carry the trailer

When a commit removes weft constructs on purpose, the hook prints the number to declare:

  or commit with: git commit --trailer "Weft-Removed: 2"

The agent adds that trailer, with that number. It does not use git commit --no-verify to get past the hook. A wrong number is refused.

A chapter’s own values go in dict_local

A value that holds for one document goes in that document’s front matter, with a why:

weft:
  dict_local:
    lab_sites:
      value: 4
      type: number
      definition: "Sites sent to the laboratory in this chapter."
      why: "Only the autumn survey sent samples away."

It is read as `r dict_local$lab_sites`. A value two documents need belongs in dict.yml (see vignette("units", package = "weft")).

Answering each kind of finding

The gate and lints() name each finding by its rule. This table says how to answer the common ones.

Finding Answer
numeral: a number typed in prose Compute it and write `r x`. If it is a choice, put it in dict.yml and write `r dict$key`. If it is quoted from a source, put it in a cite span. Only a number that is fixed by something outside the analysis, such as a method’s pore size, becomes [0.45 µm]{.weft-literal why="..."}, with a why that says what fixes it.
numeral on “Site 4” The number is a name. Ask the author to add the word to label_words in _weft.yml.
numeral on “Figure 2” Write a cross-reference, such as @fig-map.
literal-value: a value made of constants, such as `r 3 + 4` Compute it from data, or treat it as a typed number.
construct: weft syntax that does not parse Fix the syntax. The message names the rule broken.
constructs removed If intended, add the Weft-Removed: N trailer. If not, put them back.
failed claim Report it to the author. Do not edit the check or the value.
xref, anchor-twice Add the missing anchor, or rename the duplicate.
section-anchor Add {#sec-name} to the heading.
chunk-label Add #| label: name to the chunk.
figure Add the label, caption or alt text the message names.
engine Add engine: knitr to the document’s own front matter.
dict-key Use a key that dict.yml holds, or ask the author to add the entry.

A .weft-literal whose why is “fixed”, “needed” or “to pass the check” is a typed number with a label. The why is the only record of the decision, so it must say something a reader can check.

vignette("lints", package = "weft") describes every rule.

Draft mode is not a way through

draft: true in _weft.yml, or WEFT_DRAFT=1, makes a render report its failures and finish. It is for an author part-way through a chapter. An agent should not turn it on to get a render to finish, and should not leave a project in it. verify() refuses to run in draft mode, so the project cannot be checked until it is off. The commit gate still runs.

Before committing, and before handing back

  • Before a commit, run weft::lints(). It lists the findings in the project. Those that the last commit did not hold are the ones the hook will refuse. weft::gate() judges what is staged exactly as the hook will.
  • Before handing work back, run weft::verify(). It renders every document and checks every claim. A failure there is a finding to report.
  • Read weft::changes() after a render, and tell the author about each structural change and each new condition. Those are the places where a sentence elsewhere may now be wrong.
